judgment.zh_hant: 亨。利貞。可小事，不可大事。飛鳥遺之音，不宜上，宜下，大吉。
judgment.zh_hans: 亨。利贞。可小事，不可大事。飞鸟遗之音，不宜上，宜下，大吉。
judgment.en_legge: Hsiao Kwo indicates that (in the circumstances which it implies) there will be progress and attainment. But it will be advantageous to be firm and correct. (What the name denotes) may be done in small affairs, but not in great affairs. (It is like) the notes that come down from a bird on the wing;—to descend is better than to ascend. There will (in this way) be great good fortune.

tuan.zh_hant: 小過、小者過而亨也。過以利貞、與時行也。柔得中，是以小事吉也。剛失位而不中，是以不可大事也。有飛鳥之象焉，飛鳥遺之音、不宜上、宜下、大吉、上逆而下順也。
tuan.zh_hans: 小过、小者过而亨也。过以利贞、与时行也。柔得中，是以小事吉也。刚失位而不中，是以不可大事也。有飞鸟之象焉，飞鸟遗之音、不宜上、宜下、大吉、上逆而下顺也。
tuan.en_legge: In Hsiao Kwo (we see) the small (lines) exceeding the others, and (giving the intimation of) progress and attainment. Such 'exceeding, in order to its being advantageous, must be associated with firmness and correctness:'—that is, it must take place (only) according to (the requirements of) the time. The weak (lines) are in the central places, and hence (it is said that what the name denotes) may be done in small affairs, and there will be good fortune. Of the strong (lines one) is not in its proper place, and (the other) is not central, hence it is said that (what the name denotes) 'should not be done in great affairs.' (In the hexagram) we have 'the symbol of a bird on the wing, and of the notes that come down from such a bird, for which it is better to descend than to ascend, thereby leading to great good fortune:'—to ascend is contrary to what is reasonable in the case, while to descend is natural and right.

image.zh_hant: 山上有雷，小過。君子以行過乎恭，喪過乎哀，用過乎儉。
image.zh_hans: 山上有雷，小过。君子以行过乎恭，丧过乎哀，用过乎俭。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) a hill and that for thunder above it form Hsiao Kwo. The superior man, in accordance with this, in his conduct exceeds in humility, in mourning exceeds in sorrow, and in his expenditure exceeds in economy.

text.en_legge: The first line, divided, suggests (the idea of) a bird flying, (and ascending) till the issue is evil.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'There is a bird flying (and ascending) till the result is evil:'—nothing can be done to avoid this issue.

text.zh_hant: 過其祖，遇其妣。不及其君，遇其臣。无咎。
text.zh_hans: 过其祖，遇其妣。不及其君，遇其臣。无咎。
text.en_legge: The second line, divided, shows its subject passing by his grandfather, and meeting with his grandmother; not attempting anything against his ruler, but meeting him as his minister. There will be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He does not attempt to reach his ruler:'—a minister should not overpass the distance (between his ruler and himself).

text.en_legge: The third line, undivided, shows its subject taking no extraordinary precautions against danger; and some in consequence finding opportunity to assail and injure him. There will be evil.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'Some in consequence find opportunity to assail and injure him. There will be evil:'—how great will it be!

text.zh_hant: 无咎。弗過、遇之，往厲必戒。勿用永貞。
text.zh_hans: 无咎。弗过、遇之，往厉必戒。勿用永贞。
text.en_legge: The fourth line, undivided, shows its subject falling into no error, but meeting (the exigency of his situation), without exceeding (in his natural course). If he go forward, there will be peril, and he must be cautious. There is no occasion to be using firmness perpetually.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 弗過遇之、位不當也。往厲必戒、終不可長也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 弗过遇之、位不当也。往厉必戒、终不可长也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He meets the exigency (of his situation), without exceeding (the proper course):'—(he does so), the position being inappropriate (for a strong line). 'If he go forward, there will be peril, and he must be cautious:'—the result would be that his course would not be long pursued.

text.zh_hant: 密雲不雨，自我西郊。公弋取彼在穴。
text.zh_hans: 密云不雨，自我西郊。公弋取彼在穴。
text.en_legge: The fifth line, divided, (suggests the idea) of dense clouds, but no rain, coming from our borders in the west. It also (shows) the prince shooting his arrow, and taking the bird in a cave.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'There are dense clouds, but no rain:'—(the line) is in too high a place.

text.zh_hant: 弗遇、過之，飛鳥離之，凶，是謂災眚。
text.zh_hans: 弗遇、过之，飞鸟离之，凶，是谓灾眚。
text.en_legge: The sixth line, divided, shows its subject not meeting (the exigency of his situation), and exceeding (his proper course). (It suggests the idea of) a bird flying far aloft. There will be evil. The case is what is called one of calamity and self-produced injury.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He does not meet the exigency (of his situation), and exceeds (his proper course):'—(the position indicates) the habit of domineering.
